cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Reopen the First Reason
cards.instruction: Keep them present by returning to the first reason for staying and revealing that it now means something different.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the key on my table, then sit down. Returning it isn't a doorstep job.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on the table. I only came to give it back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me ten minutes as well. I want to see whether you can still visit when you have to knock.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Would you actually let me in next time?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. But next time you ask that at the door. Today you're already in, so choose a chair and tell me when you're coming back.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs key placement and sitting; A3 transforms completed return into a future-visit test; A5 grants B requested future entry while directing the present conversation.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 completed errand to reveal the relational reason; A5 directly answers B4 future entry question and keeps B present.

relationship.evidence: B2 limits the errand and B4 seeks reassurance that a future visit is welcome, a meaningful change in understanding.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4 uncertainty into permission plus a demand to plan the next visit now.

specificity.evidence: A1 key return at A home and A3 future knocking give sufficient context without inventing a breakup.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 longer reply preserves both the direct answer and concrete present request; the tone can be firm and tender.
